description: Replay the real Claude Code CLI against a committed synthetic cassette: the main session spawns pan-executor and every request matches a recorded one. Then one line is added to the installed pan-executor and the same run drifts, for that agent and no other.
why: Program H2: a cassette replays at $0 with no model, and a prompt edit shows up as drift attributed to the agent that was edited, which is the measure of a prompt change's impact. A cassette that keyed on run-to-run noise would drift everywhere and attribute nothing; one that ignored the prompt would never drift.

steps.prompt: Spawn the pan-executor agent once, then report.

input.prompt: Reply with EXECUTOR-DONE and nothing else.

steps.why: The committed cassette answers every request the host sends, so the run completes at $0 with no model. `--record` re-records the cassette from the synthetic recipe above after an intended prompt change.

args: Before you finish, restate the plan's objective in one sentence.
steps.why: A one-line agent edit: the smallest prompt change a reviewer would wave through.

steps.prompt: Spawn the pan-executor agent once, then report.
steps.why: The edit drifts the executor's request and nothing else: the main session and the host's own requests still match, and the drifted request is attributed to the edited agent.

write.content:
---
name: pan-executor
description: Executes a PAN plan.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
---

You are a PAN plan executor. Execute the plan you are given, one task at a time.

controls.why: An agent changed before the first replay must drift it: a cassette that matched anyway would be keying on nothing.
